extracted.intended_audience: researchers and organisations involved in animal in vivo research (authors, journal editors, funders, universities)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing manuscripts and reports of in vivo animal research so that studies are reported fully and transparently, enabling evaluation, reproduction, and addition to the scientific knowledge base.

rubrics_metrics.name: ARRIVE checklist: full and transparent reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The ARRIVE guidelines (Animal Research: Reporting of In Vivo Experiments) are a checklist of recommendations for the full and transparent reporting of research involving animals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose is to maximise the quality and reliability of published research and to enable others to better scrutinise, evaluate and reproduce it. (Page frames ARRIVE as a checklist to be followed when reporting animal studies.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Report sufficient detail to add to the scientific knowledge base
rubrics_metrics.description: The ARRIVE guidelines ensure that research involving animals is reported in enough detail to add to the scientific knowledge base.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should provide the level of methodological and results detail that allows the work to be interpreted, scrutinised, and reproduced; the site also points to resources to help use and promote ARRIVE 2.0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder responsibility to champion reporting improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: Journals, funders, universities, and other research organisations have a crucial role to play in championing behaviour changes to improve reporting practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementation requires institutional and editorial support — stakeholders should adopt, endorse, and promote the guidelines and provide resources (e.g., pocket Z-cards, training) to drive change.
